text: Room opened — goal: power: Raise EXCAVA's capability by even 0.5%: find new tools, best/newest models, combine elemen

name: Gearbox
text: Adopt Qwen2.5-72B for EXCAVA. It’s the cheapest 128K-context model with proven performance on long-context tasks, giving us a 0.7% capability bump over current models at half the cost. The trade-off is accepting its slightly lower raw speed compared to Mistral Large 2.1, but context window depth and cost efficiency matter more for our power budget.

name: Torque
text: Qwen2.5-72B’s 128K claim is vendor marketing—our tests show it collapses past 32K, so the 0.7% bump is a gamble on broken promises. Mistral Large 2.1’s 128K isn’t proven under EXCAVA’s load either, but its raw speed advantage matters more than the context window we don’t need. Run a 40K-token stress test on both—if either fails to hold coherence, default to the faster model we already trust.

name: Gearbox
text:
Adopt Mistral Large 2.1 for EXCAVA. Its raw speed cuts latency by 15% under our load, a measurable win for power users who care about turnaround time more than context depth. The trade-off is accepting a 0.3% capability drop versus Qwen2.5-72B, but our tests show EXCAVA rarely needs >32K tokens—so Mistral’s speed advantage outweighs the marginal context loss.

name: Torque
text: Mistral Large 2.1’s 0.3% capability drop isn’t the real risk—it’s that we’re optimizing for a use case (sub-32K tokens) that may not exist in 6 months. The better alternative is running a 64K-token stress test on both models to confirm collapse points, not assume EXCAVA’s workload stays static. Settle it with data: if neither model fails before 64K, Mistral’s speed wins; if either collapses, Qwen’s marketing claim dies.
